basics.name: Mohamed Ibrahim Aljoke
basics.summary: Backend software engineer with 4+ years of experience building distributed systems for fintech: KYC and compliance engines, customer onboarding for Banking as a Service (BaaS), and credit and payment integrations. I work mainly with Go, Node.js/TypeScript and AWS (Lambda, ECS, SNS/SQS, S3), designing event-driven architectures with asynchronous processing, the outbox pattern and infrastructure as code (Terraform). AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate, used to turning compliance requirements into domain rules and to mentoring junior developers.

projects.name: Scrap IFix Go

highlights: Built a rules-based KYC risk-scoring engine (weighted aggregation, risk catalogs, eligibility checks and watchlist mappings), turning compliance requirements into domain rules together with the compliance team.
Integrated 5 KYC, AML and antifraud data providers into automated customer onboarding: CAF Antifraude, BigDataCorp (BigBoost), BDC Sanctions, CAF Fraud History and DictStats.

Designed a client-data enrichment engine that runs synchronous and asynchronous steps in parallel, reuses previous results, matches async provider callbacks by correlation ID, and orchestrates child steps until a terminal state.
Building automated onboarding and eligibility flows for the BaaS product with domain events, the transactional outbox pattern and asynchronous integrations between services.
Process account and customer events with AWS SNS and SQS FIFO queues, using subscription filtering, deduplication and message groups for ordered, high-throughput delivery.

Designed a streaming upload path in Go (Fiber/fasthttp) for files up to ~20 MiB without loading them into memory: multipart streaming straight to Amazon S3, size-limited readers and streaming SHA-256 hashing.
Diagnosed Fiber and Sentry middleware that consumed the streamed request body before the handler, and fixed the upload path.
Built internal bulk-processing tooling to safely reprocess operational workflows at scale.

Built SEO-optimized landing pages with Next.js, real-time dashboards fed by webhooks, and a GraphQL layer with Hasura.
